title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
statement:
You start with an empty stack and a source that hands out the integers `1, 2, ..., n` in increasing order. Two operations are available:

- `"Push"`: take the next integer from the source (it must not be used up) and place it on top of the stack.
- `"Pop"`: remove the top integer of the stack (the stack must not be empty).

Return a list of operations that leaves the stack, read from bottom to top, equal to the strictly increasing array `target`. As soon as the stack matches `target`, you must stop: no further operations may follow. When several lists of operations work, any one of them is accepted.
notes:
## Intuition

Every number up to the last value of `target` has to come out of the source, because the source only moves forward. A number that belongs in `target` is pushed and kept; a number that does not belong is pushed and immediately popped. Once the last value of `target` has been pushed the stack matches, so we stop there and never read the numbers after it.

## Approach

1. Keep `current`, the next number the source will hand out, starting at `1`.
2. For each `value` in `target`, while `current` is smaller than `value`, record `"Push"` and `"Pop"` to throw `current` away, then advance it.
3. Now `current` equals `value`: record one `"Push"` to keep it and advance `current`.
4. After the last value, return `operations`; the leftover numbers up to `n` are never touched.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = [1, 3]`, `n = 3`. For `value = 1`, `current = 1` already matches, so we push it (`["Push"]`) and `current` becomes `2`. For `value = 3`, `current = 2` is too small: push and pop it, `current` becomes `3`. Then push `3`. The result is `["Push", "Push", "Pop", "Push"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m), where m is the last value of `target` (at most `n`): each number up to it adds one or two operations.
- Space: O(m) for the returned list; no real stack is needed.

## Pitfalls

- Do not loop all the way to `n`: operations after the stack matches `target` are not allowed.
- Remember to advance `current` after pushing a kept value too, not just after a discarded one.
- The value of `n` barely matters; it only guarantees the source does not run out before `target` is built.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `operations` | the list of `"Push"` / `"Pop"` steps built so far |
| `current` | the next integer the source will produce |
| `value` | the target number we are trying to place next |

narration.5: Place the target values one by one, in increasing order.
narration.6: Every smaller number from the source is not wanted...
narration.9: Move on to the next number from the source.
narration.11: Now current equals value: push it and keep it on the stack.
narration.12: The source moves past the value we just kept.
narration.14: The stack matches target after its last value, so stop and return the operations.
